blocks.value: Not every company allows the public to become owners. Companies are mainly classified as Private Companies and Public Companies.

Imagine This: Your family owns a bakery. Only your family members own it. This is similar to a private company. Years later, your bakery becomes famous across India. You invite thousands of people to invest and become owners. Now it becomes a public company.
Private companies are owned by a small group of people. Public companies allow anyone to buy ownership through shares listed on a stock exchange.
Many startups begin as private companies before becoming public companies through an IPO.
Only public companies can usually be bought and sold on the stock market.
